title: Handoff Overwrite
eyebrow: Design · two folders on one branch must not erase each other's saved work

short.lead: The desktop retest found a way to lose work. Every folder on a branch saves to one place on GitHub, refs/house-rules/autosave/<branch>. Desktop session A saved an uncommitted line there as snapshot e724bf2. Then a session in a second clone of the same branch, which had none of that work, saved its own state to the same place as snapshot 32fb8c8 and replaced A's. The pickup now finds nothing to restore. A's line still exists, but only in clone A's folder and in a local copy of the old snapshot in this repo. Nothing on GitHub holds it any more, so a second account could not get it back. The restore command fix (commit d62be1a) stays either way.
short.hint: Tap a row to see what it covers.
items: The save, the facts file and the pickup

The save runs after edits and at the end of each turn, writes a facts file into the snapshot, and pushes it. The pickup fetches snapshots when a session starts. All of this stays; only where a snapshot is stored changes.

refs/house-rules/autosave/<branch> is shared by every folder on that branch. The newest save wins, whether or not it holds the older folder's work. The pickup also preferred clone B's own newer local snapshot over clone A's on GitHub, which is why session B2 was offered nothing.
How saves from different folders are kept apart

choices: 1. How are saves from different folders kept apart?
Each folder saves under its own name: refs/house-rules/autosave/<branch>/<folder id>

The folder id is a random id written once into that folder's .git directory. A save only ever replaces its own folder's snapshot. The pickup lists every snapshot for the current branch that holds files this folder lacks, newest first, each with its own restore command. Old snapshots pile up on GitHub until removed; the save could delete its own snapshot once its folder has nothing uncommitted.
One place per branch, but a save refuses to replace a snapshot holding work it lacks

Before pushing, the save fetches the current snapshot and compares it with this folder. If the snapshot holds files this folder doesn't have, the save is skipped and says so in one line. Nothing is lost, but the second folder's own work is not saved until the first folder's work is committed.
One place per branch, each save stacked on the one before it

Each new snapshot keeps the previous one as a second parent, so older saves stay reachable from the newest. The pickup walks back through the chain to find work this folder lacks. Nothing is lost and there is one name per branch, but the chain grows with every save and the pickup gets slower and harder to read.
Each option keeps the restore command fix from commit d62be1a.

wrapup.summary: A design to stop a second folder's save erasing the first folder's saved work on the same branch.
